draft.title: Derivatives of e, log and trig
card: The derivative of e^(kx) is k e^(kx). The power stays the same and the constant k comes out the front.
The derivative of log_e(x) is 1/x, for x > 0.
The derivative of sin(kx) is k cos(kx). Angles are in radians.
The derivative of cos(kx) is −k sin(kx). Note the negative sign. Example: the derivative of cos(3x) is −3 sin(3x).
draft.remember: The constant k comes out the front each time, and cos gives a negative sin.

a.q: A function is given by f(x) = e^(6x). Which expression is f′(x)?
a.why: The derivative of e^(kx) is k e^(kx), so with k = 6 it is 6e^(6x). The option e^(6x) is tempting because e^x is its own derivative, but the constant 6 must come out the front.
a.clue: The number in front of x comes out the front.

b.q: What is the derivative of 2 cos(4x) + 3 sin(x)?
b.why: The derivative of 2 cos(4x) is 2 × (−4 sin(4x)) = −8 sin(4x). The derivative of 3 sin(x) is 3 cos(x). Dropping the negative sign for cos gives the tempting wrong answer 8 sin(4x).
b.clue: Multiply the 2 by the −4 from the cos rule.

problems.detail: "The constant k comes out the front each time" overgeneralises. The card's log rule has no k, and a student could wrongly infer that the derivative of log_e(kx) is k/x, when it is 1/x.

check.summary: Both questions and the card's rules are correct. The remember line's "each time" wrongly suggests the k rule also applies to the log derivative, which could mislead students about log_e(kx).

final.title: Derivatives of e, log and trig
card: The derivative of \(e^{kx}\) is \(ke^{kx}\). The power stays the same and the constant \(k\) comes out the front.
The derivative of \(\sin(kx)\) is \(k\cos(kx)\). Angles are in radians. In a sum, differentiate each term separately.
The derivative of \(\cos(kx)\) is \(-k\sin(kx)\). Note the negative sign. A number in front stays as a multiplier: the derivative of \(2\cos(3x)\) is \(2 \times (-3\sin(3x)) = -6\sin(3x)\).
final.remember: For \(e^{kx}\), \(\sin(kx)\) and \(\cos(kx)\), \(k\) comes out the front. \(\log_{e}(x)\) gives \(\frac{1}{x}\), and cos gives a negative sin.

a.q: A function is given by \(f(x) = e^{6x}\). Which expression is \(f'(x)\)?
a.why: The derivative of \(e^{kx}\) is \(ke^{kx}\), so with \(k = 6\) it is \(6e^{6x}\). The option \(e^{6x}\) is tempting because \(e^{x}\) is its own derivative, but the constant 6 must come out the front.
a.clue: The number in front of \(x\) comes out the front.

b.why: Each term is done separately. The derivative of \(2\cos(4x)\) is \(2 \times (-4\sin(4x)) = -8\sin(4x)\), and the derivative of \(3\sin(x)\) is \(3\cos(x)\). Dropping the negative sign for cos gives the tempting wrong answer \(8\sin(4x)\).
b.clue: Multiply the 2 by the \(-4\) from the cos rule.
